business_rules.statement: Shared mode is the predominant floor model and the tuned default, with fast switching between workers, a short configurable auto-logout, a visible who-is-logged-in indicator and identity re-confirmation at run start.
Media is evicted from the device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on the strength of an attempted upload.
Remote wipe attempts a final sync of pending captures before erasing.
A device below the application-version floor cannot be enrolled.
The application initialises its own encrypted store and never relies on the presence of mobile-device management.
Captured media never reaches the device gallery, from the first capture onward.
Remote wipe is a console critical-class action preceded by a final sync attempt, and the tenant cannot invoke it.
Configuration follows capability: enabling a capability for a tenant switches on the corresponding configuration surface in the Workflow Builder, and disabling it removes that surface.
Release Authority defaults to the Quality Manager at tenant level with a per-workflow override, and is not assigned per Service Type because nothing structural hangs on the tag.
Agent Author capability is tier-gated to Growth and Enterprise.
Every coaching asset must exist in each supported language as authored content, since nothing is machine-translated at runtime; a pack with untranslated keys fails publication.
A capability whose evaluation scenarios are pending or failing cannot be enabled for a tenant by any account.
Training Library content is excluded from every offline package.

Screen authoring uses nine configuration sections: screen content, input type, timing, gate and proof, specification limits on measurement screens only, coaching content, deviation rules and severity mapping, tool and equipment optionally, and qualification override optionally.
At least one severity mapping is required per measurement screen, because the on-device classifier must have a band to classify into.
The author writes one difficulty level, the platform's artificial intelligence drafts the other two, and every drafted level passes the full review chain before publication.
Screens hold pointers into the content libraries, and a library edit propagates to every referencing screen immediately, while a run's package is pinned at assignment and never re-based.
Validation of qualification requirements runs three times: at assignment, at run start, and when a worker reaches an override-carrying screen.

No workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of three stages: Author completes and submits; Reviewer returns or advances and cannot edit content directly; Release Authority grants final publication sign-off and cannot be bypassed.
Every republish requires a mandatory description of what changed and why, stored in permanent version history for every class, doing double duty as user-facing text for notified classes.
Approval-chain stages cannot be merged or skipped by any tenant configuration.

The package contains everything the device must render, evaluate and enforce alone: screen content at the difficulty levels in the run's locale, specification limits and gate rules, screen severity mappings with severity-catalog definitions and tenant action bundles, platform deviation-capture forms, and designated coaching defaults and short-form assets subject to device storage.
Prior versions are retained in full and remain permanently readable.

Patch versions auto-adopt and distribute without a Job Owner decision, taking effect per the tenant's adoption timing; minor and major versions are the notified classes and are decided by the Job Owner.
Each run pins its work package at assignment and the pin is immutable for the life of the run.
A package cannot be built without specification limits, severity mappings, gate rules and deviation-capture forms.

A Job is the standing definition of work and does not embed a workflow — it references one. The Job state machine is draft, then pending approval, then active, then archived, and segregation of duties is absolute: the user who creates a Job cannot approve that same Job.
Job Owner is a field on the Job, defaulting to the creator and reassignable, conferring no permissions.
Runs are optional; where a Job is executed without explicit runs the platform auto-creates a single implicit run so the record of truth never has a run-shaped hole in it.
A run left unstarted raises a supervisor alert at plus 15 minutes and is auto-cancelled at plus 30.
Exactly two in-flight modifications are permitted: worker substitution and end-time extension.
The login is the credential, not the device: a worker's identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with them onto whatever conformant device they pick up.
A worker logging in on an unexpected device is allowed at version 1 and flagged in the audit trail, with no hard block, because attribution follows the login and never the device.
No pace figure, timer against expectation or comparison to others is rendered to the worker anywhere.
Evidence is immutable at creation and bound to the step, the unit, the worker identity, the device and both timestamps.
Provenance is a named location, not a coordinate; there is no location stamp that can block a capture.
A committed capture can never be altered; corrections are append-only with who, when and what changed.
A gate blocks advance without valid proof, identically online and offline.
The Command Center is live to the server's knowledge, and it says so. Every live element shows how fresh its data is, and offline is a displayed state, never a hidden failure.
Refresh classes are pushed events within seconds of server receipt, refreshed state at a default 60 seconds configurable to a 30-second floor, and on-sync data arriving when the device reconnects.
Pace is informational and supervisor-only, evaluated at screen boundaries with a default margin of 15 per cent, and is never worker-facing.
No action on this surface can override a specification or evaluation gate, pause or stop a run, edit a record or configuration, or create Jobs or runs.
Detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device using the limits and severity mappings carried in the version-pinned work package; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.
Classification happens on-device at the instant of capture, including offline, and a Severity 1 hold is placed locally and immediately, with only the delivery of escalation waiting for connectivity.
Server-side detection atoms are the mirror and confirmation path, never the trigger.

The safety layer is not configurable: the deterministic specification gates, deviation detection, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold behave identically for every tenant, and no tenant setting, authoring choice or platform control reaches them.

The freeze lands on the Lot where a lot exists, on the Unit where work is serialized with no lot, and otherwise on the Run with its output quarantined and the run blocked pending Quality Manager disposition.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly — supervisors request release with a note, and there are no exceptions by work type, risk class or tag.
Any Severity 1 runtime event automatically creates a Critical anomaly in the register, and a Critical anomaly notifies the Tenant Admin and the Quality Manager.
No timer, agent or escalation ever releases a hold.
Downstream-consumer hold propagation — reaching forward to assemblies that already consumed material from a held lot — is a defined later extension and not launch behaviour.

A waiting gate item follows the same acknowledge, timeout and fallback discipline as any escalation, with defaults of a 10-minute window at Severity 1 and 30 minutes otherwise; it never executes on its own and it never silently expires.
No agent classifies a deviation, releases a Severity 1 hold, self-approves or bypasses any gate.
Full traces are retained 24 months platform-internal, and a derived decision record — plan summary, atoms invoked, gate outcome and approver — persists with the operational record for its full term.
Notification channels are in-app and email only, platform-wide, at every tier, and in-app notifications cannot be muted.
An unacknowledged Critical notification re-notifies the same audience on the same channels after four hours, tightening to one hour in Regulated-Industry mode.
A notification never enforces a hold, a qualification block, an authorisation, an approval, a suspension or a device command.
Sync is continuous when connected, resumes automatically on reconnection and is never a worker action; a manual sync control exists only as a convenience, never as a dependency.
Server-receipt time is authoritative for ordering at sync, and clock skew beyond the tenant threshold is flagged so a materially wrong device clock is visible rather than silently trusted.
A designated high-risk action such as a sign-off forces a sync first, so authority is never recorded from stale cache.
There is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run; a supervisor releasing a hold reaches the worker at the next sync.
Command channel classes are exactly five: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension and version change.
Conflict resolution is automatic — the most recent write wins by the device-side timestamp — and the full conflict event is audited; the panel is a review instrument, never a blocker.
A skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed and is excluded from Resolve All.

A conflict whose two values disagree beyond the screen's specification limits is passed to the rule-based deviation mechanism, because two materially different readings of the same capture is a quality event and not bookkeeping.

The rework loop is captured in full with multiple cycles and the append-only record preserves the entire story: the original failure, what was done, and every eventual pass, with nothing ever overwritten.
Launch genealogy is one level of as-built links plus the full rework history; multi-level walkable genealogy is a later extension.
Pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker, and the substitute receives a structured handover of last completed step, open flags and current state.
Worker-finished is what stands a run as submitted; complete-and-synced is what moves it to complete.

Acknowledgement of the shift handoff brief is an explicit timestamped action distinct from merely opening the brief, and never blocks a shift from starting; an unacknowledged brief flags on the Plant Manager view after a configurable grace period, default 30 minutes.
Cross-shift work is not supported as a single run at version 1; it is modelled as two linked runs with a structured handover step reserved between them.
The finish is the one automatic transition on the platform — a data-integrity rule rather than a status change — firing after a tenant-configurable window with a default of 48 hours.
Late captures arriving inside the window fold in flagged late_arrival and are rejected after it; data from a worker archived in the interim is still accepted within the window, dual-flagged.

Corrections after finish are append-only annotation records and, where they materially change computed figures, trigger an audited recompute with the prior output preserved, a late-data indicator on the Summary and a notification to the reviewing Quality Manager.

Aging highlights fire at 24, 48 and 72 hours and the queue appears in the per-shift digest; the platform enforces no review service-level agreement — the aging highlights and digest are the pressure, not a lock.
Three named access classes exist and only three: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.

Sessions expire at the configured time-box, default two hours; the tenant can terminate the session from the banner at any time; cross-tenant access events additionally mirror into the affected tenant's own audit stream, giving one audit truth per tenant.

The emergency pause suspends agent activity platform-wide or per tenant; in-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park, raised gates stay human-decidable, and resume is a separate audited act. It renders as agent unavailability, never silence, and it never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.

An atom or agent whose scenarios are pending or failing cannot be enabled, and an enabled one whose evaluations start failing is flagged immediately; the gate is shown as enforced and has no off position for any role including the root.

decisions.question: Does device enrollment belong to the Super Admin console (§7.5.2) or is it tenant self-service through the Delivery Operations Hub (§8.13.4)?
options: tenant self-service enrollment within platform policy
decisions.adopted_working_position: this chapter shows the tenant enrolling within platform policy because that reading is the more specific of the two
decisions.impact: Determines who owns device enrollment, mode setting and location binding.

decisions.question: What is the client's standardised device profile?
options: working floor of a sensible mainstream Android and iOS specification
decisions.adopted_working_position: until they land, the working floor is a sensible mainstream Android and iOS specification
decisions.impact: Sets the published minimum device specification.

decisions.question: What scanner hardware list does the client standardise on?
decisions.impact: Determines hardware scanner vs camera fallback expectations.

decisions.question: What is the device behaviour when on-device storage fills with unsynced evidence?
options: deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification
decisions.adopted_working_position: Not specified in the Statement of Work; no behaviour may be invented here. Constraints: may not discard unsynced evidence, may not weaken the gate, may not allow work producing unrecordable captures.
decisions.impact: Terminal safe state for storage-full is undefined.

decisions.question: Is per-tenant atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval (§8.2.2) or an Admin action (§8.19)?
decisions.impact: Decides who may switch a capability on for a tenant.

decisions.question: Which wins between a global disable and a tenant-specific override?
decisions.status: open — this chapter does not choose
decisions.impact: Precedence of capability enablement.

decisions.question: Does the Prevention Agent operate under pre-authorised policy (§3.7, §6.6.1) or must every action agent route through a human gate (§8.3.2, §8.3.3)?
options: runtime human gate for every action agent
decisions.adopted_working_position: the gate form is declared per agent on the agent record — `authoring-time policy` for the Prevention Agent, `runtime human gate` for the Deviation and Containment Agent's proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, and `none — reasoning agent` for the Shift Handoff Agent and every tenant-composed agent
decisions.impact: Determines whether coaching cards need a runtime human gate.

decisions.question: How many modules does the Standards and Operations Studio have?
decisions.adopted_working_position: The Studio module count is `Derived Clarification`
decisions.impact: Module inventory for the Studio surface.

decisions.question: Which seven capture types does the screen-element contract name — §1.7/§7.8.3's set or §5.5.3's set?
options: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature and free text
measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or quick-response scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text and dropdown selection
decisions.adopted_working_position: the set the contract now names is the adopted §5.5.3 seven, so dropdown selection is authorable and a multi-item proof step is authored as a checkbox confirmation carrying several items
decisions.impact: Fixes the renderable capture-type set a player must draw.

decisions.question: What happens to an in-flight run whose containment checklist or coaching asset changes mid-run — immediate propagation or pinning?
decisions.status: open — this chapter does not choose
decisions.impact: Whether a library edit reaches a running package.

decisions.question: How does the three-stage approval chain reconcile with Lane B's auto-publish?
decisions.impact: Whether an approved Lane B change bypasses the chain.

decisions.question: Does the package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's level?
decisions.adopted_working_position: until it is resolved the package definition carries all levels
decisions.impact: Package size and offline difficulty-level availability.

decisions.question: Which fields are package-borne and which are server-only?
decisions.adopted_working_position: stated to live in the package contract but is not enumerated in the source
decisions.impact: Authoritative field-by-field package contract.

decisions.question: Is one Area per Job a hard constraint (§4.5.1) or is it one parent node per Job at the configured depth (§2.1)?
options: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
decisions.adopted_working_position: §2.1's — one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
decisions.impact: Job-to-location binding granularity.

decisions.question: What is the Plant Manager persona's authority on the Client Command Center?
options: full Quality Manager authority where that role is also held
decisions.adopted_working_position: the Plant Manager persona's authority here is read and escalate unless the Quality Manager role is also held, so the audit trail is always honest about which authority made a call
decisions.impact: Whether a Plant Manager can decide gates or release holds.

decisions.question: Who receives an escalation when nobody holding the target role is on shift?
options: fallback to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback
decisions.adopted_working_position: delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, explicitly marked as a fallback — recommended
decisions.impact: Escalation never resolves to no one.

decisions.question: On reconnection, does a device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
options: Option C: stop-class commands, then captures, then enabling classes
decisions.adopted_working_position: stop-class commands — suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation and remote wipe, and any tenant compliance stop — apply first; the full capture queue then uploads; the enabling classes of lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance and version change apply last
decisions.status: adopted at Option C; ratification rests with the client with JBS engineering input
decisions.impact: Never leaves a suspension behind a queue and never leaves evidence behind a command.

decisions.question: What happens to a wipe command that cannot be delivered to an offline device?
decisions.adopted_working_position: a wipe command would sit pending and cannot be delivered
decisions.impact: Undeliverable stop-class command semantics.

decisions.question: How are scrap, use-as-is and return-to-supplier dispositions modelled, given the Statement of Work defines no scrap state?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the recommendation is anomaly closure categories at version 1 with unit states scoped as an extension; the decision owner is the client's quality lead
decisions.impact: Whether a scrapped unit has a first-class state.

decisions.question: Is a missed shift-handoff brief regenerated for the elapsed shift?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the recommendation is not to backfill a brief, because a handover note produced after the handover has happened is misleading rather than useful
decisions.status: not specified in the Statement of Work
decisions.impact: Scheduled-work misfire semantics.

decisions.question: Are the record-finish window's floor and ceiling settled at 24 hours and 7 days, or is that an open drafting value?
decisions.impact: Bounds on the tenant-configurable finish window.

decisions.question: What are the five standard report data sets, and which name for set four is correct?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the identity of the five standard report data sets is open with the client
decisions.impact: Report Builder data-set inventory.

decisions.question: What happens when the support-session banner cannot render in the tenant's user interface?
options: block session opening until the banner is confirmed rendered
decisions.adopted_working_position: the recommendation is to block opening until the banner is confirmed, since it fails safe without interrupting an engineer mid-diagnosis; the decision owner is the client's platform lead
decisions.impact: Whether a support session may remain open without tenant visibility.

contradictions.description: §7.5.2 describes device enrollment and lifecycle as belonging to the Super Admin console while §8.13.4 makes enrollment tenant self-service.
conflicting_values: tenant self-service enrollment through the Delivery Operations Hub (§8.13.4)

contradictions.description: §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval while §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes, including feature enablement, Admin actions.
conflicting_values: Platform Engineer change riding the approval cycle (§8.2.2)

contradictions.description: §3.7 and §6.6.1 describe the Prevention Agent as operating entirely under pre-authorised policy while §8.3.2 and §8.3.3 describe every action agent as routing through a human gate.
conflicting_values: runtime human gate before any effect (§8.3.2, §8.3.3)

contradictions.description: §1.7 and §7.8.3 name one set of seven capture types while §5.5.3 names a different set of seven; both are called seven and the sets differ.
conflicting_values: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature and free text (§1.7, §7.8.3)
measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or quick-response scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text and dropdown selection (§5.5.3)

contradictions.description: One Area per Job is stated as a hard constraint in §4.5.1 while §2.1 recasts it as one parent node per Job at the configured depth.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth (§2.1)

contradictions.description: The three-stage approval chain conflicts with Lane B's auto-publish of an approved change to a package-borne value.
conflicting_values: explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority
never auto-approved, automatically published, fully audited

contradictions.description: A global disable and a tenant-specific override are a genuine precedence question the source does not settle.

Whether a reconnecting device uploads pending captures before or after pulling pending commands is never fixed in the Statement of Work; safety argues commands first, data integrity argues captures first.
conflicting_values: commands first, because a suspension, wipe or hold must land before more work is done
captures first, because unsynced evidence should never be put at risk by a command that might lock or wipe the device

contradictions.description: Library pointers propagate immediately to every referencing screen while a run's package is pinned at assignment; the in-flight interaction is unresolved.
conflicting_values: a library edit propagates to every referencing screen immediately
a run's package is pinned at assignment and never re-based

contradictions.description: The record-finish window's floor and ceiling are stated as settled at 24 hours and 7 days in §4.6.8 and §8.19 and as an open drafting value in §2.4.
Report data set four is named differently in §4.10.5 and §6.12.1.
The Statement of Work defines no scrap or disposition state, though a manufacturer will expect scrap, use-as-is and return-to-supplier dispositions to be first-class.
The source requires the support-session banner to show for the whole session but does not state what happens if the banner cannot render.
conflicting_values: block session opening until the banner is confirmed rendered

controls.label: retire control
controls.effect: Retires the device from the fleet with its history preserved.

controls.label: manual sync control
controls.effect: Convenience only; sync is never a worker action or a dependency.

controls.label: publish control
controls.effect: Mints the version after chain, version-number and locale checks.

controls.label: approve or return controls
controls.effect: Approves publication or returns with reasons.

controls.label: manual archival control with a no-active-Jobs indicator
controls.effect: Deliberate archival of a version; never automatic.

controls.label: read-only formatted export
controls.effect: Exports a version document for training and regulatory submission.

controls.label: per-section mute controls and no service-level mute
controls.effect: Users mute sections of the digest, never services.

controls.label: forward-only navigation control with read-only access to prior screens
controls.effect: Advances only when the gate's proof is present.

controls.label: approve
controls.effect: Executes the agent's proposed intervention as authored.

controls.label: adjust within bounds and approve
controls.effect: Executes an adjusted scope, recorded as a learning signal.

controls.label: decline with a categorised reason
controls.effect: Declines the proposal; the pattern is proposed less often.

controls.label: Resolve All
controls.effect: Accepts the most recent version of every ordinary conflict; excludes skew-flagged items.

controls.label: flag-as-wrong control
controls.effect: Opens the append-only correction path rather than altering the sync result.

controls.label: explicit acknowledgement control with its timestamp
controls.effect: Records acknowledgement; never blocks the next shift starting.

controls.label: per-item annotation controls
controls.effect: Marks a brief item stale or corrected; feeds the output-feedback loop.

controls.label: manual Portable Document Format export control
controls.effect: Exports the Execution Summary manually.

controls.label: export controls for comma-separated-values and JavaScript Object Notation formats
controls.effect: Exports audit data with date and entity filters.

controls.label: re-send-on-material-correction option
controls.effect: Re-sends a corrected report flagged as a correction.

controls.label: End-session control
controls.effect: Terminates the support session immediately, resolving in the tenant's favour.

controls.label: scope selector of platform-wide or per tenant
controls.effect: Sets the blast radius of the emergency pause.

controls.label: separate resume control that is its own approved action
controls.effect: Resumes agents from their checkpoints; never implied by the pause expiring.

controls.label: eligibility indicator showing whether the viewer may act
controls.effect: Hides stages barred by separation of duties.

controls.label: per-screen comment control
controls.effect: Returns comments to the Author; the Reviewer cannot edit content.

controls.label: filters by Area, severity, type and state
controls.effect: Filters the alert and escalation feed.

controls.label: role-scoped filters by Job, Site, Area and Worker
controls.effect: Filters the run schedule within the viewer's scope.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the device cannot complete enrollment because it cannot reach the platform
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retry enrollment on a working connection; the device remains unenrolled and unusable in the interim
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the device is below the minimum specification or the application-version floor and can never enroll as it stands
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the device is not enrolled, holds no tenant data, and cannot receive a package; no worker can start a run on it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: update the application or replace the hardware, then enroll

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a capability the tenant needs is not enabled, so its configuration surface never appears
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the Platform Engineer submits per-tenant enablement into the approval cycle and an Admin approves it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the capability's evaluation scenarios are pending or failing, so it cannot be enabled at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the workflow cannot be authored with that capability's configuration; no partially configured screen may be published
failures_fallbacks.recovery: platform engineering brings the scenarios to passing, the enablement is approved, and the surface appears

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the author needs a capture type the screen-element contract does not name
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: author the intent with one of the seven — a multi-item proof step is a checkbox confirmation carrying several items, and a constrained choice is a dropdown selection
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the operation genuinely needs a construct none of the seven expresses, such as video capture or a Bluetooth-gauge reading, both of which are roadmap
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the screen is not authored with the unnamed type and the workflow is not published with it, because a player cannot render a type the contract does not name
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the roadmap item is raised as a scope change, or the client ratifies or reverses DEC-CAP-001 and the screen-element contract is reissued

failures_fallbacks.trigger: no eligible Reviewer exists because the only other grant-holder authored the submission
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the Tenant Admin layers an authoring grant on a second qualified person
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: no second person is available at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the submission stays submitted and unpublished, no version exists, no package can be built, and no Job can link to it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: a second grant-holder is provisioned and the review proceeds

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the package build fails because a referenced coaching asset is missing from the content library
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the version publishes without that optional coaching asset if coaching is not required for the screen
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the missing item is a specification limit, a severity mapping, a gate rule or a deviation-capture form
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the package is not built and the version is not distributable; the prior version, if any, stays in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore the missing element in the Studio, which requires a new submission through the full chain if the element is content rather than a library pointer

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the pre-sync fails and the package does not reach TAB-014 before the shift
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: lazy pull when the device is next connected, plus an on-demand re-pull the supervisor can request
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the device does not regain connectivity before the shift starts
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the run cannot be entered; the worker is shown a not-yet-ready run rather than an empty or partial one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: connectivity returns, the package lands, and the run becomes ready

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the digest fails to deliver by email because the vendor rejects the message
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the in-app notification, which cannot be muted and back-fills on login, carries the same content
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the worker never opens the application inbox, which is permitted because general notifications carry no read obligation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the qualification block still applies at expiry, enforced at step level on the device, whether or not any warning was ever read
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the failed email is reconciled and the next stage warning fires on schedule

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the hardware scanner fails to read a serial
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the camera, since scan-to-identify uses the hardware scanner where present and falls back to the camera otherwise
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: neither reads the mark, for example because the label is damaged
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the unit is not identified, so no Unit Execution opens and no capture binds to a serial
failures_fallbacks.recovery: platform-assigned identity where the operation creates identity on the line, or a re-labelled part

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the board's refresh cycle stalls, so state aggregates stop updating
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the board continues to render the last known state with its ageing as-of stamp
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the session loses its push channel as well, so events also stop arriving
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the board shows an explicit degraded state naming what it can no longer see, and the supervisor is directed to the record of truth in the Delivery Operations Hub
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the session re-establishes, aggregates recompute, and pushed events replay from the server

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the device's storage fills, so a capture or its evidence cannot be committed locally
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, so no unsynced evidence is discarded to make room; the device reports pressure rather than deleting
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: storage remains full with unsynced evidence held
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: not specified in the Statement of Work; deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification as DEC-STORE-001. Constraints: may not discard unsynced evidence, may not weaken the gate, may not allow work to continue producing unrecordable captures
failures_fallbacks.recovery: connectivity returns, the queue drains, media is evicted after confirmed receipt, and pressure clears

failures_fallbacks.trigger: no Quality Manager is on shift when the escalation delivers
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, explicitly marked as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: no Quality Manager responds at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the lot stays frozen; the Critical anomaly stays open and the unacknowledged Critical notification re-notifies after four hours, or one hour in Regulated-Industry mode. A frozen lot is a safe state; an unreleased lot is never released by a timer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: a Quality Manager acts and releases, or the tenant escalates outside the platform

failures_fallbacks.trigger: an agent run fails and no brief is produced
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the deterministic record stands on its own and the human decides from it; a missing brief never blocks a decision
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the agent fails a second consecutive time or the failure outlasts a shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: agent unavailability is displayed honestly rather than as silence, the escalation reaches the Plant Manager view, and every deterministic control continues untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the agent is fixed through a Studio or platform action linked from the panel

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the email vendor rejects a Critical escalation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the in-app notification, which cannot be muted, carries the same content to every open session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: nobody holding the routed role is on shift, so there is no session to reach
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and is visibly marked as a fallback; the underlying hold or block remains in force throughout
failures_fallbacks.recovery: a person acknowledges and acts

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the device's clock drifts beyond the tenant's skew threshold of approximately five minutes
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the platform orders that write by server-receipt time instead and flags it as skew-affected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the skew-flagged write would otherwise win a conflict
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: a skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed — the record carries the unflagged version until a Quality Manager resolves the conflict individually, and skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the Quality Manager resolves the conflict individually in SEQ-024

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the connection drops part-way through the drain
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the durable resumable queue continues where it left off when connectivity returns
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: an individual capture repeatedly fails validation at the server
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: that capture is quarantined — held for review, visible, and never silently discarded — while every other capture proceeds; the run's summary shows the gap honestly
failures_fallbacks.recovery: a Quality Manager reviews the quarantined item and either accepts it, triggering an audited recompute, or records why it cannot be accepted

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the conflict panel is overwhelmed by a large backlog after a long multi-device outage
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resolve All accepts the most recent version of every listed ordinary conflict in one action
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: many conflicts are skew-flagged and are therefore excluded from Resolve All
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: skew-flagged conflicts remain individually reviewable, the unflagged version stands on each record until reviewed, and work continues throughout because the panel is never a blocker
failures_fallbacks.recovery: individual review clears the flagged set

failures_fallbacks.trigger: rework cannot bring a unit into specification after repeated cycles
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the loop repeats, with each cycle recorded, because the platform imposes no cycle limit
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the unit is not recoverable by rework at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the unit's execution record shows an unbroken chain of failures with no pass, the associated anomaly stays open until a Quality Manager records a closure note, and the unit is never marked as passing; the Statement of Work does not define a scrap state (DEC-SCRAP-001)
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the closure note and the disposition

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the Shift Handoff Agent run fails and no brief is produced
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the incoming supervisor reads the underlying deterministic records directly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the agent fails a second consecutive time or the failure outlasts a shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the failure escalates to the Plant Manager view, the panel keeps showing the honest per-tenant flag, and the shift starts regardless because no shift ever waits on a brief
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the agent is fixed through a Studio or platform action linked from the panel, and the next scheduled occurrence runs; backfill is not specified (DEC-SCHED-MISFIRE-001, recommendation: do not backfill)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the run auto-close scheduler misfires because its host is unavailable during the maintenance window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the durable queue re-drives the occurrence on the next tick, preserving the original due time on the record so the delay is visible
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the re-drive fails because the Summary recompute cannot complete while a capture is quarantined
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the run stays complete and is never finished early; late data continues to be accepted; the countdown prompt continues; platform operations is alerted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the quarantined capture is resolved, the Summary recomputes with the prior output preserved, and the occurrence executes, finishing the run with the delay recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the session banner fails to render in the tenant's user interface
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: not specified in the Statement of Work; raised as DEC-SUPPORTVIS-001 with a recommendation to block opening until the banner is confirmed rendered
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the session remains open with no tenant visibility
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the session's actions are still mirrored into the tenant's audit stream and appear on Platform Access History, so visibility is delayed rather than lost, and the session expires at its time-box regardless
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the banner renders on the tenant's next page load and the End-session control returns

failures_fallbacks.trigger: an enabled capability's evaluation scenarios begin failing in production
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: per-tenant pause where the blast radius is contained
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the degradation spans tenants
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform-wide emergency pause, which renders as honest agent unavailability with every deterministic control intact and every raised gate still human-decidable; the floor keeps running
failures_fallbacks.recovery: remediation through maker-checker, scenarios returning to passing, and a separate audited resume
